message: Hi, I'm a student with a full stack certification background. My overall academic average is 76.2% in an IT/computer-science degree. I'm interested in programming and system developer. I want to become a Technical Engineer. My family can afford at most about USD 4000 per year. I live in Mumbai. I'm open to going abroad. Getting a good job after graduation matters more to me than anything else.
reflection_note: The original shortlist was strong but included PR0194, which is outperformed by the newly added PR0161. I dropped PR0194 because its placement metrics are weak relative to its cost and technical focus. PR0161 (MSc Software Engineering) is a much better fit for the student's core goal ('Technical Engineer/Programming') than PR0194, while still respecting the CS background requirement. The final list prioritizes low-cost, high-employability options that align with either pure development (PR0161) or general IT skills (PR0195, PR0021).
explanation:
Keystone School of Engineering
This program was recommended because it offers a very low annual tuition of $300, fitting well within your maximum budget. It has an excellent placement rate of 82% and provides an 18-month post-study work visa, supporting your high employability priority. The main trade-off here is that the focus on "business_information_systems" may be less purely technical than desired for a core programming role, despite its strong career outcomes.

Ashford Institute of Technology
This option aligns strongly with your budget constraints, featuring an annual tuition cost of only $450. It boasts a high placement rate of 82% and offers the valuable 18-month post-study work visa, making it excellent for immediate employment prospects. The trade-off is that its focus on "it_support" suggests a more operational role rather than deep system development, which might deviate slightly from your technical engineering goal.

Keystone University
This program maintains a low cost with an annual tuition of $550 and provides the desired 18-month post-study work visa. It is suitable for students interested in how technology interacts with users, as its focus is on "design_hci." The main trade-off to consider is that this specialization leans heavily into design rather than core programming, and it has a slightly lower placement rate of 78% compared to other options.

Tejas University
This program is the most technically aligned option for your goal, as it is an MSc in Software Engineering and requires a CS background matching your academic profile. While its annual tuition of $3850 is higher than the others, it remains within your $4000 budget limit. The primary trade-off is that while highly relevant to development, this program has the lowest median starting salary ($33,731) and placement rate (72%) among the shortlisted options.
